payload.exhibitionTitle: Constructed Worlds: Architectural Visions from Piranesi to Wright
payload.curatorialRationale: This exhibition explores the representation of architectural space across cultures and centuries, from 18th-century European classicism to 20th-century American modernism. Caillebotte's monumental 'Paris Street; Rainy Day' serves as the anchor, capturing a fleeting urban moment. It is flanked by two thematic pairings: one wall juxtaposes Piranesi's classical etching with Sargent's impressionistic watercolor of Venice, exploring European perspectives. The opposing wall creates a dialogue between the organic modernism of Louis Sullivan and Frank Lloyd Wright and the Japanese spatial concepts seen in Hiroshige's print, which profoundly influenced their work. The selection deliberately balances a single, durable oil painting with five light-sensitive works on paper, creating a varied visual rhythm and addressing conservation needs.
